newsitem.title: USA: Ratings gap between HK and China to persist -- S&P.
newsitem.headline: Ratings gap between HK and China to persist -- S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said the three-notch differential between its sovereign ratings of Hong Kong and China takes into account foreseeable risks after the July handover.

Major risks to Hong Kong after the transfer of sovereignty, such as potential misgovernance or a detoriaration in China's credit fundamentals, have already been factored into Hong Kong's A-plus foreign currency credit rating, S&P said in a teleconference.
"Abstracting from the China factor, Hong Kong would be rated very high in the double-A category at least," said Lacey Gallagher, director of sovereign ratings.
Gallagher said S&P believes China will respect Hong Kong's autonomy for "three basic reasons."

Hong Kong is the major source of foreign investment in China, it is a conduit for the country's foreign trade and it is seen as a proving ground for the one-country-two-systems model China hopes to implement eventually in Taiwan, she said.
Asked if Hong Kong and China would share a single currency in the foreseeable future, Gallagher said: "We would expect the timetable to be 50 years at least."
"As long as it would be necessary for the next 50 years or more, we fully expect the Hong Kong dollar to remain the official currency of Hong Kong," she said.
On Wednesday, S&P upgraded China's foreign currency credit rating to BBB-plus from BBB and revised the country's ratings outlook to stable from positive.
